title: Esra's Algorithm Adventure
markdown:
Sunrise exploded through the observatory. Today was the Galactic Games. The Constellation Maze: light beams, gravitational traps, a colossal puzzle. The prize: funding for Esra’s nebula research. Her stomach churned. She mapped galaxies, not mazes.

Mica, her sleek sable cat, blinked. Mica didn’t worry. Esra sighed. “This maze is too much. How do I find the right path?”

Captain Noor’s voice cut through. “Esra. Ready for the final briefing? The maze tests your ability to think. Most stumble through with luck.”

Esra gulped. Luck would not fund her work. She watched Noor stride away, then gazed at Mica. The cat stretched, then moved. Mica wasn’t staring at the whole jumble. She focused on the next clear space. She wove through tubes and wires, one small obstacle at a time. Dart. Pause. Select. Dart again.

A thought hit Esra. It was not about seeing the single perfect path from the door. It was about building a path, piece by piece. Smart decisions at each junction, from what was in front of you.

The maze was a sequence of decisions. She grabbed her datapad. A branching diagram. Junction A: if the beam is red, go left; if blue, go right. A trap? Then the next rule. Mapping a phenomenon. A precise process. A logical sequence. An algorithm.

The Games bell chimed. Esra took a breath. Mica gave a soft encouraging chirp. Esra stepped onto the platform. Blinding beams. Traps shimmered. She was not lost. She was following her rules. “Left.” Boots on the next platform. “Next junction: check the sensors.” Mica’s paw-taps a rhythm. Each decision small, efficient, logical.

She dodged a simulated asteroid field by applying the next rule to its heading. She bypassed a swirling gravity well with short leaps, like Mica from table to chair. Heart hammering. Not running the maze. Solving it.

The finish line: a cascade of glittering starlight. She stepped through. The crowd erupted. Captain Noor appeared, beaming. “Esra. Incredible.”

Esra grinned, panting. “Mica showed me. Break it down. One step at a time. Then the next.”

Noor nodded. “What you designed is an algorithm. A set of clear instructions for a complex problem. Logic, in sequence. The same kind of thinking that plans a route, or a procedure in the lab.”

Esra looked at the conquered maze, then at Mica, grooming a paw. An algorithm. Not only for mazes. For charting a nebula, for anything that looked too big until you named the next step. A new set of possibilities, already opening. She did not declare the day amazing. She scratched Mica’s ear, and wondered what other puzzles would yield if she wrote the rules first.
characters: Esra (an astronomy intern), Mica (a cat), Noor (a captain)
